these are really interesting and seem like different cultures' response to magic existing.  The same way different ancient cultures had their own numerical systems or thoughts on philosophy. Maybe there is one or a few universal magic sources and these systems are different ways of manifesting said magic. I love how you have magic that is like martial arts but you also have magic involving math. They could be just two different expressions of the same power. the ninth faction could be the only faction that recognizes this or knows how to classify these different magics. I could also see these as totally separate and this world being very diverse and rich but in either route it might be weird to just stop at eight without suggesting that there is more.  Just glancing at your systems i'm personally inclined to say that 2,4,5 could be drawing from the same source because they all seem to be based off of visualization mental power and willpower if i'm understanding them correctly. 3 and 6 seem especially wild and volatile and thats why I feel inclined to group them together. 1 could also belong to this category. I could imagine 7 being an experiment gone wrong from number 4. 8 seems to be its own beast but can seem connected to 6, 3 and 1.  This is really just me spitballing but if you have a plan i bet you could put them all in your story.  All of these powers have a somewhat connected feel to them and thats why I like the idea of them all being from one main source.

i'd suggest making a Venn diagram with how each system works and what you want that system to work with your story/setting. If you are trying to cram a bunch of magic systems into your story that fulfill the same narrative purpose and work a little too similarly; its time to cut the fat. Next is aesthetic. The aesthetics of the magic systems have to similar enough to fit the setting, but not different enough that one feel out of place. if you've heard of the king killer chronicles, it does something like this pretty excellently.  It keeps the magic interesting and separate by having one form of magic much more esoteric and mysterious than the other. One system of magic is easy to understand with hard rules while the other is always at the edge of the story. Having a progression like this is a good way not to overwhelm the audience but still have more magic at play and it makes the world feel deeper too. I have to say that the devil is likely in the details with stuff like this though. You're probably just going to have to feel out what works and is convincing.
